title: Happy Number
statement_short: Determine if a positive integer n is happy. Starting with n, replace the number by the sum of the squares of its digits, repeating until the number equals 1 or loops endlessly in a cycle.
hint: Number value range limits do not restrict time complexity; cycle detection in digit sum sequences requires fast and slow pointers.
keywords: sum of the squares of its digits
why_not: Right: Linked List (Fast & Slow) applies Floyd's cycle detection to identify sequence repetition in O(log n) time and O(1) space. Not HashMap / Hash Set: Using a set to track seen numbers detects cycles in O(log n) time but uses extra O(log n) memory. Not Math / Geometry: Hardcoding known cycle numbers works, but fast & slow pointers generalize cycle detection algorithmically. Not 1D DP: Storing state transitions uses extra space for deterministic sequence generation.
